name: GlobalsDB
tagline: InterSystems' free NoSQL release of the Caché globals engine (c. 2011–2016), with Java, Node.js and .NET APIs.
description: GlobalsDB was a free download from InterSystems that exposed only the storage kernel of Caché: globals, persistent sparse multi-dimensional arrays addressed by a variable name plus any number of subscripts. It left out SQL, the object layer, ObjectScript, ECP distribution and the rest of Caché, and gave developers a native API first for Java, then Node.js and finally .NET, so any key-value, document or tree layout could be modelled directly on the sorted global structures. InterSystems used it to introduce MUMPS-style storage to a wider developer audience. The project faded after 2015 and its domain was later taken over by unrelated sites. InterSystems IRIS, including its free Community Edition, is the successor.
statusNote: Discontinued by InterSystems around 2016; globalsdb.org now hosts unrelated content. InterSystems IRIS is the successor.

pricing.notes: Was a free download with no registration; no longer offered.

scale.notes: Single-node engine; the distributed ECP layer of Caché was not included.

strengths: Same globals storage engine that powers Caché and IRIS deployments
Sorted multi-dimensional arrays model key-value, tree and document data directly
Very low-latency native access from Java and Node.js
weaknesses: Discontinued and no longer downloadable from InterSystems
No SQL, objects or secondary indexing beyond what you build into globals
useCases: Historical context for InterSystems IRIS and MUMPS-style storage
notIdealFor: New development (use InterSystems IRIS Community Edition or YottaDB)
